crossStoryFindings: The derived-view pagination change is only partially propagated: shared contracts, route/schema wiring, the derived-view service, PlatformStore implementations, and several test doubles no longer agree on the `listDerivedArchiveViews` request/response shape.

Turn and derived-view cache behavior now diverges between the in-memory test store and the Convex production store, so cross-story reopen behavior is not being validated against the real persistence path.

Archive capture, turn derivation, and derived-view surfaces are conceptually aligned around archive truth, but the default execution path that feeds the archive is still a canned runtime-audit script rather than real process-specific execution.
architectureFindings: The tech design says turn and derived-view rebuilds happen on read from canonical archive data; the current services only rebuild when the cached first page is empty, which is weaker than the documented contract.

The architecture expects Fastify pagination contracts to match store and durable-layer contracts end to end; the current derived-view rollout breaks that consistency and fails the type gate before tests can run.
Canonical archive truth is supposed to preserve finalized process work, but the default production executor still synthesizes archive entries from a hard-coded audit payload.
epicCoverageAssessment: `corepack pnpm run verify-all` fails in `typecheck`, so none of the Epic 7 service, client, integration, or e2e tests actually execute to green.

The added Story 6/7 tests around detached-source degradation and bounded derived-view pages improve intended coverage, but they currently provide no passing evidence because the build is broken first.
Static inspection found a production-only stale-cache path that the in-memory tests mask, so even a later green test run should explicitly verify Convex-backed reopen/read behavior.
productionPathFindings: The production app wires `new ScriptExecutionService(providerAdapterRegistry)` by default, and that service's default payload factory emits a synthetic integrated runtime-audit script that fabricates `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `model_message`, `process_event`, and `script_emission` archive entries.

`InMemoryPlatformStore` deletes cached turns and derived views on archive append/patch, but `ConvexPlatformStore` does not, so production can serve stale derived data even though the primary test store self-heals.
No equivalent fake adapter was found in the archive read routes themselves; the material non-real execution paths are the canned script executor and the test-only cache invalidation behavior.

blockingFindings.title: Derived-view pagination refactor is incomplete and breaks the epic gate
blockingFindings.evidence: Running `corepack pnpm run verify-all` fails in `typecheck` before any Epic 7 tests run. The current rollout leaves `DefaultDerivedArchiveViewService` and multiple store/test implementations disagreeing about the `listDerivedArchiveViews` shape: TypeScript reports `'cursor' does not exist in type '{ processId: string; }'`, `'views' does not exist on type 'DerivedArchiveView[]'`, plus contract failures in `tests/service/server/processes-api.test.ts`, `tests/service/server/auth-routes.test.ts`, and `tests/service/server/derived-archive-view.test.ts`.

blockingFindings.title: Convex production reads can return stale turns and derived views after new archive entries arrive
blockingFindings.evidence: `DefaultTurnDerivationService.getTurns` rebuilds only when the first cached page is empty, and `DefaultDerivedArchiveViewService.listViews` now does the same. In production, `ConvexPlatformStore.appendArchiveEntry` and `patchArchiveEntry` only write archive rows; they never clear `archiveTurns` or `derivedArchiveViews`. By contrast, `InMemoryPlatformStore` explicitly deletes those caches on append/patch and after turn upserts. After the first successful rebuild, later archive appends in Convex can leave `/archive/turns` and `/archive/derived-views` stale indefinitely until an explicit refresh.

blockingFindings.title: The default production archive capture path still archives a canned runtime-audit script, not real process execution
blockingFindings.evidence: `apps/platform/server/app.ts` constructs `new ScriptExecutionService(providerAdapterRegistry)` when no override is injected. The default `ScriptExecutionService` payload factory always returns `buildIntegratedRuntimeAuditPayload`, whose hard-coded TypeScript module writes a runtime report and emits synthetic archive entries for `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `model_message`, `process_event`, and `script_emission`. That means the live production path feeding Epic 7 is still a placeholder execution program rather than real process-specific work.

crossStoryFindings: Archive entry reads and turn derivation are mostly intact, but the derived-view slice is currently broken: `tests/service/server/archive-api.test.ts` passed 15/15 and `tests/service/server/turn-derivation.test.ts` passed 8/8, while `tests/service/server/derived-archive-view.test.ts` now fails 6 of 7 cases with 500s.

The archive/turn/view layers no longer react consistently to provenance-only degradation. `/archive` re-enriches entries per read, but cached turns/views can stay stale after source detachment or related-context loss.
architectureFindings: A partial derived-view pagination refactor drifted across layers. `DefaultDerivedArchiveViewService` expects paged stored-view reads, but lower store/Convex seams and several callers still assume the older array-returning contract.

Derived projections are only invalidated on archive writes. Source/artifact state changes do not invalidate or recompute `archiveTurns` / derived views, so the rebuildable-projection contract no longer matches the archive read path's degraded-state behavior.
epicCoverageAssessment: Archive append/read, access checks, and turn derivation still have meaningful coverage: `archive-api.test.ts` passed 15/15 and `turn-derivation.test.ts` passed 8/8 when run directly.

Derived-view coverage is red. `derived-archive-view.test.ts` fails TC-5.1a, TC-5.2a/5.3a/5.3b, the degraded-on-reopen scenario, TC-7.1b, bounded paging, and the derived-view cache invalidation scenario.
Epic 7 is not green end-to-end because Story 5/7 behavior is down and the turn/view degraded-state contract is inconsistent with Story 6 provenance degradation.
productionPathFindings: The live derived-view read path is materially broken right now. `corepack pnpm vitest run tests/service/server/derived-archive-view.test.ts` returns 500s for the GET `/archive/derived-views` scenarios, so the structural-view surface is not usable.

Turn and derived-view caches are not refreshed when only related provenance changes. A source detachment can change `/archive` output immediately while `/archive/turns` and cached derived views keep serving pre-detachment readiness.

blockingFindings.title: Derived-view read path is broken by a partially applied pagination contract change
blockingFindings.evidence: `corepack pnpm run typecheck` reports `apps/platform/server/services/archive/derived-archive-view.service.ts(254,48)` because `listAllStoredViews` is still calling `platformStore.listDerivedArchiveViews({ processId })` while the new signature requires paging, and `tests/service/server/derived-archive-view.test.ts(417,61)` / `tests/service/server/processes-api.test.ts(341,5)` show callers still returning arrays instead of `{ views, page }`. Running `corepack pnpm vitest run tests/service/server/derived-archive-view.test.ts` now yields 6 failing 500s, and `corepack pnpm vitest run convex/archiveEntries.test.ts` still fails the derived-view primitive expectations.

blockingFindings.title: Cached turns and derived views do not re-derive when provenance degrades after the archive is written
blockingFindings.evidence: `DefaultArchiveReadService` re-enriches archive entries on every read (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-read.service.ts:52-65` plus `apps/platform/server/services/archive/archive-entry-enrichment.ts:10-152`), but `DefaultTurnDerivationService.getTurns` only rebuilds when the cached turn page is empty (`apps/platform/server/services/archive/turn-derivation.service.ts:87-98`). I reproduced this by building turns, detaching the linked source attachment, and calling `getTurns` again; the second response still returned the original `ready` turn. The derived-view service follows the same cache-first pattern, so reopen behavior can diverge between `/archive`, `/archive/turns`, and cached derived views after source detachment or provenance degradation.

unresolvedItems: Both named gates are failed, but neither completed a clean full sweep: `corepack pnpm run green-verify` and `corepack pnpm run verify-all` stopped immediately in `format:check` on `convex/derivedArchiveViews.ts`, so the remaining lint/build/integration stages were not reached in a passing run.
The provenance-staleness regression was reproduced manually at the service layer; there is no current automated regression test covering cache refresh after source detachment.
